Advogato Flow

Advogato admits an account when 1 unit of integer network flow reaches it from a small set of trusted seeds. The flow moves along certifications. Each account has a capacity, and the capacity decreases with the distance from the seeds. Draw a graph, select the seeds, change the schedule, and step through the computation. The text on the right always describes the picture on the left.

    Each account at each threshold

    Account Seed Distance Capacity c(v) Consumed Forwarded Result Apprentice Journeyer Master Reported level

    Distance, capacity, consumed, and forwarded apply to the selected threshold. The reported level is the highest threshold at which the account is accepted. tmetric_run records this value. It runs the metric one time for each level, and each higher accepted level replaces the lower one.

    How the computation works
    1. Select a certification threshold: Apprentice, Journeyer, or Master. Keep only the certifications at that level or higher. In tmetric_run, a certification at level L goes into the flow graphs of all levels from 1 to L. Thus the Master graph is part of the Journeyer graph, and the Journeyer graph is part of the Apprentice graph.
    2. Connect a synthetic source to each trusted seed. The source is a node with the name -. The metric creates it first, so it has index 0. The reference treats it like all other nodes. It is at distance 0, it gets caps[0], and it uses 1 of those units on its own sink edge. Thus the metric can accept at most caps[0] − 1 real accounts.
    3. Do a breadth-first search from the source. Each reachable node gets a distance d and a capacity c(v) = caps[d]. After the last entry of the schedule, the last value continues. A node with no certification path from a seed is not reached. It keeps capacity −1 and gets no trust.
    4. Split each node v into vin and vout. Add 3 types of edge: vin → vout with capacity c(v) − 1, vin → shared sink with capacity 1, and, for each certification u → v, uout → vin with no capacity limit. The 1 unit that a node can send to the sink is the unit that admits it. The other c(v) − 1 units are all that it can forward. In net_flow_max_flow, this is the TWEAK: capacity[i]-- for each node, and a node_sink value of 0 or 1 for each node. The split is necessary because a flow can only limit edges, and certification edges must stay unlimited. The split changes the capacity of the account into 1 edge that each unit must cross, with no regard to the number of certifications.
    5. Compute an integer maximum flow from the source to the shared sink. The reference finds augmenting paths with a breadth-first search over the residual graph (net_flow_augment). The search moves forward along a certification, through a node that has forwarding capacity, and backward along an edge that already carries flow. The backward move lets the search re-route a unit to make room for a new one. The first in-node that the search reaches with an empty sink edge gets the next unit.
    6. Accept each account that has 1 unit on its sink edge. Each accepted account uses exactly 1 unit. Each unit that reaches the sink admits exactly 1 account. The total flow is the number of accepted accounts, plus the source.
    7. Do this again for each threshold. For each account, report the highest level at which it is accepted. The 3 runs are independent maximum flows. Thus an account can be accepted at Master and lose a tie at Journeyer. The reference reports Master, because each higher level replaces the lower one.

    Modeling choices and simplifications
    • Kept from the reference:
      • The synthetic source is node 0, and it reserves 1 unit for itself.
      • Capacity comes from the BFS distance, and the last schedule entry continues.
      • Each node is split into in and out, with c(v) − 1 on the through-edge and 1 on the sink edge.
      • Augmenting paths come from a breadth-first search in the same order as net_flow_augment.
      • The metric runs one time for each level and reports the highest accepted level.
      • Self-certifications are removed, as net_flow_init_graph removes self-edges.
    • Simplified: the reference first makes a greedy tree (net_flow_assign_tree) and starts the flow from it. This simulator starts from zero flow. The maximum flow value is the same. The set of accepted accounts can be different, because a maximum flow is not unique. A tie-break is not a trust judgement. The traversal order here is the order in which the accounts and the certifications were created. The reference reads the accounts from a directory. The same input always gives the same result, but the winners of a tie are an effect of the order.
    • Schedule entries must be 1 or more. The reference reads its schedule up to the first zero, so a zero cannot occur inside it. A capacity of 1 means that the account can be accepted, but it forwards nothing.
    • Labels are not inputs. The scenario labels fake, bad, confused, and attacker are for the reader. The metric sees only accounts, certifications, and seeds. It does not know which accounts are malicious.
    • Out of scope: Advogato has a separate diary-rating system with a different computation. This simulator does not model it. The editor keeps 1 certification for each pair of accounts, as an Advogato profile does.

    Compared with EigenTrust
    Advogato (Levien)EigenTrust (Kamvar, Schlosser, Garcia-Molina)
    OutputAn integer admission set. Each account is in or out, one time for each level.A continuous reputation vector t with a sum of 1. The accounts are ranked.
    MechanismA maximum flow through capacities that decrease with the distance from the seeds.Power iteration of normalized local trust, mixed with the pre-trusted peers.
    FormulaAccept v if the sink edge of vin carries 1 unit in a maximum flow.tnext = (1 − α) C⊤ t + α p
    Role of the seedsThe source feeds the seeds. Capacity is a function of the distance from them.The pre-trust vector p, uniform over the seeds. A peer that trusts nobody uses p.
    What a cluster of fakes getsAt most the units that cross the cut into the cluster. This is a count.The share of the score that flows in, divided among its members. This is a fraction.

    Same graph, same threshold, same seeds as pre-trusted peers

    AccountEigenTrust scoreAdvogato result

    Here each certification at or above the threshold is a local trust value of 1, normalized for each certifier. The paper does not give a value for α. This page uses 0.15 as the default. Advogato has a separate diary-rating system with a different computation. It is outside the scope of this simulator.

    Sources
    • tmetric.c: the certification graph of mod_virgule and the run for each level: the source node -, the seeds, the thresholds, and the report of the highest level.
    • net_flow.c: capacity assignment by breadth-first search, the in/out split (TWEAK), and the augmenting-path maximum flow.
    • The EigenTrust Algorithm for Reputation Management in P2P Networks: Kamvar, Schlosser, and Garcia-Molina, WWW 2003.
    • Jesse Ruderman, "Advogato's trust metric is not attack-resistant" (2005): the distance-shortening attack in the fourth scenario.
    • mod_virgule (Raph branch): the full Advogato code base, GPL.
